name: Mansi
notes: Northern (Sosva) Mansi, Ob-Ugric branch, Khanty-Mansi Autonomous Okrug, Russia. INPUT CONTRACT: modern Sosva Mansi Cyrillic orthography, NFC. Long vowels are spelled with a combining macron over the base vowel letter (⟨а̄ о̄ э̄ ӣ ӯ⟩); short/long is therefore a real orthographic contrast, not free variation, so the macronised letters are separate grapheme keys (Riese 2001, Sec. 1.1-1.2). ⟨в⟩ is the labio-velar approximant /w/ (Riese 2001), not Russian /v/. The native (non-loanword) consonant inventory has no plain voiced obstruents (⟨б в г д ж з⟩ occur only in Russian loans; Riese 2001, Sec. 1.3) — their values here are the loanword pronunciation. The coronals ⟨л⟩, ⟨н⟩ and ⟨т⟩ palatalise before the iotated vowels ⟨е ё и ю я⟩ and the soft sign ⟨ь⟩ (Riese 2001; directly evidenced by NorthEuraLex нёл -> ɲ o l and питьми -> p i tʲ m i), so those sequences are entered as multigraph keys the maximal-munch matcher prefers over the bare consonant. Word stress in Mansi is fixed on the first syllable and therefore not phonemically distinctive (Riese 2001, Sec. 1.4); this is documented as an stress encoded (fixed initial, Riese 2001) (a fixed, non-contrastive position needs no per-word marking) rather than modelled with a stress schema. ITERATION FIX (error-analysis pass against NorthEuraLex): ⟨а⟩ corrected to /a/ (not /ɐ/) and ⟨а̄⟩ to /aː/ (not /ɑː/); ⟨э̄⟩ to /ɤː/ (NorthEuraLex э̄ӈын -> ɤːŋɪn); ⟨х⟩ to the uvular /χ/, with the labialised clusters ⟨хв⟩ /χʷ/ and ⟨кв⟩ /kʷ/ entered as multigraphs (NorthEuraLex эква -> əkʷa, ахвтас -> aχʷtas — the labialisation is not a separate /w/ segment); ⟨ы⟩ to /ɪ/ (distinct from the /ə/ of ⟨ы⟩'s reduced-vowel neighbour, matching NorthEuraLex лылыйэ̄п -> lɪlɪjɤːp); the palatal digraphs for ⟨л⟩/⟨н⟩ from the PHOIBLE-sourced fronted allophones /ʎ̟/ /ɲ̟/ to the plain /ʎ/ /ɲ/ that NorthEuraLex's transcription consistently shows (e.g. паль -> paʎ, аня -> aɲa); and a parallel /sʲ/ palatalisation series added for ⟨с⟩ before the same iotated-vowel/soft-sign environment (ся̄нь -> sʲaːɲ). Classification and coordinates follow Glottolog.
